questions.explanation: The trap is: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4. Place value decides instead: 0.4 is 0.40, forty hundredths, which is more than twenty-five hundredths, so 0.4 is bigger than 0.25.
questions.misconception: Comparing decimals by digit count: 0.25 looks bigger than 0.4 because 25 > 4.

questions.explanation: Scene s3 lines up the places: write 0.4 as 0.40, then forty hundredths plus twenty-five hundredths is sixty-five hundredths, so 0.4 + 0.25 = 0.65.

questions.answer: 0.4 = 0.40: four tenths is the same amount as forty hundredths, because ten hundredths make one tenth.
questions.explanation: Scene s3 shows the extra zero arriving: zeros on the right of a decimal change nothing - 0.4 and 0.40 name the same amount in different places.
questions.prompt: Write 0.4 in hundredths and explain why the value does not change.

questions.explanation: Scene s2 shades the square column by column: two full columns are twenty hundredths and five more tiny parts join them, making 0.20 + 0.05 = 0.25.
questions.prompt: How many hundredths are in 0.25? Split your answer into tenths and hundredths.

questions.explanation: Convert to hundredths first: 3 tenths is 30 hundredths, and 30 + 15 = 45 hundredths, which is 0.45.
